description: Issue #970: EtlPipelineExecutor.BulkLoadWithRetryAsync's retry catch converts a cancellation observed at the exact instant the loader throws a transient (non-cancellation) failure into OperationCanceledException, via `cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` checked FIRST inside the catch, before deciding retry vs. give up. Without it, that catch falls through to `if (attempt >= maxRetries) { throw; }`, re-throwing the transient exception's OWN type unchanged -- past the OperationCanceledException-only catch above it (which cannot match a non-cancellation exception type) -- all the way to the caller's general `catch (Exception ex)`, which reports an operator-cancelled run as an ordinary data failure (Aborted=false) instead of an abort. This mutant removes exactly that one `cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();` line, reproducing the pre-#970 defect verbatim. Checked against RetryWithBackoffTests.Cancellation_already_requested_when_transient_thrown_aborts_immediately, which cancels synchronously inside MockBulkLoader.OnBeforeTransientFailureThrown (fired immediately before the loader throws its simulated transient failure), so cancellation is deterministically already requested by the time the retry catch runs -- with the mutant applied, Aborted comes back false and the assertion fails. The green controls are unrelated to this specific line: Single_transient_failure_recovers_with_one_retry proves ordinary retry-then-succeed is unaffected; Cancellation_during_retry_backoff_aborts_immediately proves the OTHER cancellation interleaving (during the Task.Delay backoff wait, caught by the separate `catch (OperationCanceledException)` immediately above the mutated line) is untouched by this mutant; Failures_beyond_budget_abort_job_with_retry_count proves the non-cancelled, retries-exhausted `attempt >= maxRetries` give-up path -- reached by the same catch block, just past the removed check -- still classifies a genuine data failure as Aborted=false.
target_symbol: EtlPipelineExecutor.BulkLoadWithRetryAsync -- the `cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();` call at the top of the retry catch block
